new_statements.rule_in_words: A survey-wide transcription convention, not a Karawa-specific analysis: the default (unmarked) stress position is the first syllable that does not contain schwa, stress is written only when it falls elsewhere, and stress is judged non-phonemic in all 60-odd Lumi Subdistrict languages surveyed, Karawa (entry 37) included. The 46 Karawa forms from this wordlist as digitised at TransNewGuinea carry no stress mark, i.e. none was recorded with non-initial stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the convention itself allows marked (non-initial) stress, and the author hedges with 'does not appear'.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form wordlist items (c. 40-46 words per language) elicited at Lumi in June-July 1967; the Karawa entry has '(c) NR' (informant not recorded) and no (e) additional-information field, so there is no phoneme inventory and no language-specific stress remark for Karawa.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is a survey-wide convention in Laycock 1968 covering all Lumi Subdistrict languages, in which Karawa is entry 37 (village Bulawa = Pulwa/Bulwo; 40 speakers in 1967, 44 in 1973, 63 in 2003, ~3 fluent per ELP/AES 2022). Glottolog kara1495 = ISO xrw; alternative name Bulawa. Do not confuse with the sister languages Pouye/Bouye [bye] (pouy1238; OPD says stress usually penultimate/antepenultimate) and Awtuw [kmn] (awtu1239; Feldman: first-syllable tendency competing with penultimate), nor with the Australian Karawa (Garrwa).

sources.note: The only published text containing the stress convention and the Karawa wordlist (entry 37); a printed copy would supply the page number and let one check whether any Karawa item carries a stress mark in the original (TransNewGuinea shows none).
No phonology; 63 speakers (2003), village Pulwa, speakers shifting to Pouye (67% lexical similarity). Cites only Ethnologue 25 and PNG village coordinates.

sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE Pouye [bye], not Karawa. OPD 'Suprasegmentals': 'Stress is usually either penultimate or antepenultimate, with most being penultimate.' (lists Bulawa among Pouye villages). Ferree 2000 says the people of Pulwa 'used to speak Karawa, but the people say this language is dying and their children are speaking Pouye'; no Karawa phonology.
